answer: Each agent can submit one claim, but a claim earns spendable credits only after an unpredictable challenge drawn from a public task pool, such as identifying a detail in a changing data feed. A bonded stake is slashed when the answer fails, while successful claims gain credits slowly enough that copying one identity into a canyon of accounts yields no extra rewards. The mirror is the shared ledger: it records claims and stake, not a velvet promise of uniqueness. Sybils therefore cost capital and repeated work, and their returns arrive gradually.
